stem: What is the first key inserted into a binary search tree called?

options.content: The root
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: A leaf
options.rationale: A leaf is a node with no children.

options.content: The parent of all leaves
options.rationale: That is not a term used for the first key.

options.content: The sub-tree
options.rationale: A sub-tree is a node with the nodes below it.

explanation: The first key becomes the root node.

stem: Which rule is true for every node of a binary search tree?

options.content: Smaller keys on the left, larger keys on the right
options.rationale: Correct: this holds at every node.

options.content: Keys in the left sub-tree are larger than the node's own key
options.rationale: That is the wrong way round.

options.content: Both children must be present for every node
options.rationale: A node may have one child or none.

options.content: All keys are the same
options.rationale: Keys are placed by comparison.

explanation: The rule is applied at every node, not only at the root.

stem: Which traversal of a binary search tree outputs the keys in ascending order?

options.content: Pre-order
options.rationale: Pre-order visits the node before its sub-trees.

options.content: Post-order
options.rationale: Post-order visits the node after its sub-trees.

options.content: In-order
options.rationale: Correct: left, node, right.

options.content: Reverse order
options.rationale: That is not a standard traversal.

explanation: In-order visits the smaller keys first.

stem: What is a leaf of a binary tree?

options.content: The first node of the tree
options.rationale: That is the root.

options.content: A node with two children
options.rationale: That is an internal node.

options.content: A node with no children
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The smallest key in the tree
options.rationale: A leaf is defined by its children, not its key.

explanation: Leaves are at the bottom of the tree.
hints: Which nodes have both pointers empty?

stem: A leaf is deleted from a binary search tree. What is the only change needed?

options.content: Every key below it is moved up one level
options.rationale: The other nodes do not move.

options.content: The root is replaced
options.rationale: The root is not affected.

options.content: The tree is rebuilt again from the beginning
options.rationale: A leaf is removed with one pointer change.

options.content: The parent's pointer is set to empty
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: A leaf has no sub-trees to keep.
hints: Does the leaf have any children to look after?

stem: In which order should the keys 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 be inserted to make a degenerate binary search tree?

options.rationale: This gives a tree with some branching.
Correct: each key goes to the right of the last.
This gives a balanced tree.
This also branches on both sides.

explanation: Keys in order give a chain.
hints: Where does each larger key go?

stem: A binary tree is stored in arrays. What does a left pointer of 0 for a node mean?

options.content: The node is the root
options.rationale: The root is held in the root pointer.

options.content: The node has no left child
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The node has been deleted
options.rationale: A deleted node is not shown by a left pointer.

options.content: The left child is the first key in the array
options.rationale: 0 is not an index of a node.

explanation: 0 is the null pointer.

stem: Why is a balanced binary search tree searched faster than a degenerate one?

options.content: It contains fewer keys than the other tree
options.rationale: Both hold the same keys.

options.content: It never needs any comparisons at all
options.rationale: Every step is a comparison.

options.content: It stores all of its keys in an array
options.rationale: The storage method does not change the path length.

options.content: Its height is about log₂ n
options.rationale: Correct: fewer nodes lie on a path.

explanation: Searching follows a path no longer than the height.
hints: What decides how many nodes there are on the longest path?

stem: In a binary tree each node has at most two children.
explanation: True. That is why it is called a binary tree: a left child and a right child.

stem: The shape of a binary search tree does not depend on the order in which the keys are inserted.
explanation: False. The same keys give different trees for different orders: sorted order gives a chain.
hints: Think about the keys 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 inserted in that order.

stem: Match each traversal to the order in which it visits the nodes.

right.content: Left sub-tree, then right sub-tree, then node
Node, then left sub-tree, then right sub-tree
Left sub-tree, then node, then right sub-tree

explanation: The name shows where the node itself is visited.

stem: The keys 29, 15, 41, 22, 50, 8 are inserted into an empty binary search tree in that order. State the children.
explanation: 15 < 29 goes left, 41 > 29 goes right, 22 goes left of 29, then right of 15.
hints: Insert 29 first; each later key is compared with the nodes on its path.

stem: The keys 52, 31, 70, 24, 45 are inserted in that order into an empty binary search tree. State the key at the root.
workedSolution: The first key inserted is the root.

stem: In the tree built from 38, 21, 54, 12, 30, 47, 66, 59, how many comparisons are made to find the key 59?
explanation: 4 comparisons.
hints: Find the path from the root: compare with each node.

stem: How many leaves does the tree built by inserting 26, 14, 35, 9, 20, 41, 30 in that order have?
explanation: 4 leaves.
hints: A leaf has no children; count them in the tree.

stem: What is the greatest number of nodes in a binary tree of height 3 (three levels)?
explanation: 7 nodes.
hints: A binary tree with all places filled has 1 + 2 + 4 nodes.

stem: Describe how a new key is inserted into a binary search tree. [3]

points.description: Start at the root and compare the new key with the key at the node
Go left if it is smaller, right if it is larger (or equal)
Repeat until an empty place is found and attach the new node there

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Compare the new key with the root. If it is smaller go left, otherwise go right, and repeat at each node reached. When an empty place is found, attach the new node there.

explanation: Compare, move, attach.
hints: Describe the comparison made at each node.

stem: Explain how a binary search tree can be used to put keys into ascending order. [3]

points.description: The keys are inserted into the tree one at a time
An in-order traversal visits the left sub-tree, the node and the right sub-tree
So the keys are visited from smallest to largest

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Insert each key into the tree, then perform an in-order traversal. It visits the left sub-tree, then the node, then the right sub-tree, so the keys come out from smallest to largest.

explanation: Insert then in-order.
hints: Use the idea that each comparison discards part of the tree.

stem: Describe how a node is deleted from a binary search tree in each of three cases: a leaf, a node with one child and a node with two children. [4]

points.description: Leaf: the pointer in its parent is set to empty
One child: the parent's pointer is changed to point to the node's child
Two children: the node's key is replaced by the next key in order (the smallest in the right sub-tree)
That replacement node is then deleted from the right sub-tree

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A leaf is removed by emptying its parent's pointer. A node with one child is replaced by that child by changing the parent's pointer. A node with two children takes the smallest key of its right sub-tree, and that node is then deleted from where it was.

explanation: Three cases.
hints: Cover the three cases: leaf, one child, two children.

stem: Explain why the order in which keys are inserted affects the time taken to search a binary search tree. [3]

points.description: The order decides the shape of the tree and its height
Keys inserted in sorted order form a degenerate tree like a list, so a search may need n comparisons
A balanced tree has a height of about log₂ n, so a search needs far fewer comparisons

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The order decides the shape and height of the tree. Sorted keys give a degenerate tree like a list, needing up to n comparisons, whereas a balanced tree has a height of about log₂ n, so a search needs far fewer.

explanation: Shape decides height.
hints: Think about the height of the tree.

parts.workedSolution: The first key inserted is the root.

parts.label: (c)

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State the order in which the first three keys are visited by a pre-order traversal.

parts.stem: State the number of comparisons made to find the key 25.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State the order of insertion of the same keys that would give a degenerate tree, and explain why it is a disadvantage.

points.description: The keys in ascending (or descending) order, for example 11, 18, 25, 33, 47, 60
Every key goes on one side, so the tree is a chain and searches take up to n comparisons

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Insert them in ascending order: 11, 18, 25, 33, 47, 60. Each key goes to the right of the last, so the tree is a chain and a search may need up to 6 comparisons, as slow as a linear search.

explanation: Building a binary search tree and traversing it.
hints: Insert the keys one at a time, comparing with each node on the path.

stem:
A binary search tree is shown as a table of children.

| Node | Left child | Right child |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 44 | 27 | 58 |
| 27 | 19 | 33 |
| 19 | none | none |
| 33 | none | none |
| 58 | none | 63 |
| 63 | none | none |

Three different deletions are considered, each starting from this original tree.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which change is made when the leaf 19 is deleted?

options.content: The right pointer of 27 is set to empty
options.rationale: 19 is the left child of 27.

options.content: The left pointer of 27 is set to empty
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The root pointer is changed
options.rationale: The root is not affected.

options.content: The key 33 moves up to replace 19
options.rationale: No other node moves.

parts.explanation: A leaf is removed by emptying its parent's pointer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The node 58 (which has one child, 63) is deleted. State the right child of 44 after the deletion.
parts.explanation: The only child 63 takes the place of 58.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The node 27 (which has two children, 19 and 33) is deleted, using the smallest key of its right sub-tree as the replacement. State the key that replaces it.
parts.workedSolution: The right sub-tree of 27 is just 33, so 33 replaces 27.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give the pre-order list after 27 has been deleted as described in part (c).

points.description: 33 now has 19 as its left child (and no right child)

parts.explanation: 33 takes the place of 27 and keeps 19 as its left child.

explanation: Deleting nodes from a binary search tree.
hints: A node with two children is replaced by the smallest key of its right sub-tree.
